name: East Micronesia Cable System - Kosrae cable landing station
developer: East Micronesia Cable System consortium; NEC supply/installation contractor; DXN modular CLS supplier
notes: EMC landed at Kosrae (Sep 2025, final Pacific location) and NEC official press (2026-05-15) states construction was completed and the system handed over to FSMTCC/BNL/Cenpac; AIFFP and project site corroborate. Landing stations house optical transmission and power feed equipment - telecom infrastructure, not commercial colocation/DC. No commercial DC found for Kosrae (searched data center/colocation/EMC terms 2026-08-12).

name: Digital FSM - Secure Government Network and Data Center / Government Cloud (FSM-Cloud)
developer: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia (DTCI/Digital FSM Office); World Bank/IDA funding (P170718, US$30.8M)
notes: Digital FSM (World Bank P170718) includes Secure Government Network and Data Center, Disaster Recovery/Business Continuity and Government Cloud (FSM-Cloud) components per ESMP and project documents; World Bank results story (2026-07-07) tracks new digital services hosted on private-sector-operated green data centers with a target of 3 by March 2027. Project lead until procurement/commissioning names a site and operator; likely Palikir/Kolonia (Pohnpei) but not confirmed.

name: East Micronesia Cable System - Pohnpei cable landing station
developer: East Micronesia Cable System consortium; DXN Limited modular CLS
notes: DCD reported the Pohnpei CLS delivered in March 2025; EMCS spans ~2,250 km connecting Tarawa/Nauru/Kosrae/Pohnpei and integrates at Pohnpei with the HANTRU-1 trunk (BU3). Cable landing station houses optical transmission/power-feed equipment - telecom infrastructure, not commercial DC.

name: FSMTC international gateway and HANTRU-1 cable-landing facilities (Kolonia/Pohnpei)
notes: FSMTC (TRA Individual Operating License IL-001) operates international gateway and submarine-cable/cable-landing facilities; HANTRU-1 Pohnpei-Guam upgrade completed 2021 (fsmtc.fm); FCC DA-09-1309A1 documents HANTRU-1 ownership/IRU structure; TRA register confirms license class and FTTP rollout in Pohnpei. Telecom/gateway infrastructure; no public colocation product.

name: FSMTCC/CableCorp (OAE) wholesale colocation at central offices/exchanges
developer: FSM Telecommunications Cable Corporation (FSMTCC/CableCorp, a.k.a. OAE)
notes: TRA market-entry page and OAE wholesale overview PDF design colocation space, power and cooling at central offices/exchanges plus future colocation/backhaul products; CableCorp is the government-owned wholesale-only open-access entity (TRA license IL-002), HQ Ocean View Plaza (East Wing) Suite 15, Pohnpei. Treat as planned/wholesale telecom colocation until a live tariff or service order confirms availability.

name: Chuuk-Pohnpei submarine cable - Weno/Chuuk landing station
notes: C-P cable to Pohnpei operational since 2019-04-27 with a Chuuk landing station (per FSMTCC/TRA records); FSMTC outage notices confirm operational dependence and FSMTCC/OAE maintenance windows; TRA identifies FTTP in Weno as a bottleneck facility. Telecom infrastructure, not commercial DC; CPUC/iSolutions remain licensed telecom leads only (no facility evidence).

name: Chuuk State Solar Server Education Hub (iSolutions)
developer: iSolutions; APNIC Foundation ISIF Asia grant
notes: APNIC Foundation project page (checked 2026-08-12) documents a small solar-powered school connectivity/server hub completed under a 2014-2015 ISIF Asia infrastructure grant. Community server-room/education ICT infrastructure, not a commercial data center; recorded for completeness.

name: Boom! Inc. (iBoom) Colonia data center / central office
notes: APNIC Foundation technical report (checked 2026-08-12): Boom! built out a data center/central office in Colonia, secured up to 20G IP transit/backhaul and connected it to Yap's cable landing station. TRA licenses Boom! Inc. (P.O. Box 215, Colonia Yap FM 96943) for terrestrial cable, international gateway and satellite earth-station facilities. Small telecom central office/DC, not hyperscale or carrier-neutral colocation; capacity undisclosed.

name: Yap Spur / SEA-US submarine cable landing station
notes: Yap's spur to SEA-US in service since late June 2018; TRA market page confirms CableCorp holds an IRU for the Yap Spur; FSMTCC Yap page documents open-access fiber/FTTP build on Yap Proper; FSMTC FTTP on Yap Proper is a TRA-identified bottleneck facility. Cable/telecom infrastructure, not commercial colocation.
